reason: The dispersion book did its job through the 10-14 to 10-16 semiconductor selloff: eight of nine longs are up on the leg (CME +6.0%, CI +6.7%, DG +6.2%, MCK +5.1%, TRV +4.8%), the 34.5% SPY short is up 1.9%, and no stop fired. Research (WebSearch, limited coverage of the past week) supports the hard-data legs: CME reported record September ADV of 31.8M contracts (+22% y/y) and record Q3 ADV of 29.4M (+16%), led by Treasury futures and options (+42%), so the largest leg's thesis is confirmed before its Q3 print; TRV has already reported a strong Q3 (core EPS $9.18, combined ratio 86.8%, record net investment income), which removes that event risk. The one loser, AKAM (-13.6% against an -18% stop), slid on margin and estimate-revision worries with no single new event I could find; Q3 earnings are Nov 5. Its idiosyncratic drawdown is the kind of uncorrelated residual a dispersion basket expects to hold, and the standing stop caps it, so I am not crystallising the loss or paying churn to rotate. SLB reports Oct 23, a name-specific catalyst that fits the mandate. Drift since entry leaves longs near 52.4% of NAV against a ~32.9% SPY short. That is still roughly beta-neutral after the Blume adjustment, so re-hedging would cost more in frictions than it would correct. Holding the book, stops and take-profits unchanged.
